title: Malignant Hyperthermia — Crisis Protocol
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: Malignant Hyperthermia
MHAUS / EMHG 2024 dantrolene dosing update; MHAUS emergency protocol

changelog.change: Initial entry — trigger agents, early signs, and the MHAUS crisis sequence: dantrolene, stop triggers / switch to TIVA, active cooling, treat the metabolic consequences, 24-h ICU for recrudescence.

summary: A hypermetabolic crisis of skeletal muscle triggered by volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine in a susceptible patient (RYR1 / CACNA1S). A rising EtCO₂ despite adequate ventilation is the earliest reliable sign. Call the MHAUS hotline (US): 1-800-644-9737. Give dantrolene immediately and do not stop looking for it.

items: TRIGGER: all volatile agents (sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane, halothane) and succinylcholine.
SAFE: propofol, ketamine, etomidate, opioids, benzodiazepines, non-depolarising NMBs, nitrous oxide, local anaesthetics, dexmedetomidine.
Unexplained rising EtCO₂ despite increasing minute ventilation — the first reliable sign.
Masseter spasm after succinylcholine, then generalised rigidity.
Tachycardia, tachypnoea, then a rapid temperature rise (> 1 °C per 5 min) — fever is often LATE.
Mixed metabolic + respiratory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, myoglobinuria, later rhabdomyolysis and DIC.

rows: 2.5 mg/kg IV rapid bolus → repeat the FULL 2.5 mg/kg q5 min PRN (MHAUS/EMHG 2024 — not 1 mg/kg) until EtCO₂, HR, rigidity, and temperature respond. Usual max ~10 mg/kg (up to 20 mg/kg if refractory — reconsider the diagnosis beyond that). Ryanodex 250 mg/vial reconstitutes far faster than the older 20 mg/vial dantrolene.

Stop the volatile. Switch to TIVA (propofol ± opioid). Hyperventilate with 100% O₂ at ≥ 10 L/min. Get help; assign someone to mix dantrolene (each 20 mg vial needs 60 mL sterile water). Change the circuit and CO₂ absorber when time allows (do not delay dantrolene for this).
Ice to the groin / axillae / neck, cold IV fluids, gastric / bladder / peritoneal lavage with cold saline, cool open cavities. STOP cooling at 38.5 °C (overshoot to hypothermia).

Bicarbonate for acidosis (guided by ABG). Hyperkalaemia: calcium, insulin + dextrose, albuterol (see the hyperkalaemia module). Amiodarone for ventricular arrhythmias — AVOID calcium-channel blockers with dantrolene (hyperkalaemia, cardiovascular collapse). Maintain urine output > 1–2 mL/kg/hr; alkalinise the urine for rhabdomyolysis.

Dantrolene 1 mg/kg IV q4–6 h for ≥ 24 h (bolus preferred over infusion — allows reassessment). Recrudescence occurs in ~20%, a median of ~9 h after the initial crisis — watch for returning rigidity, rising EtCO₂, rising CK. Monitor CK, BMP, coags, and urine q6–8 h; CK peaks at 12–24 h. Refer the patient AND family for RYR1 genetic testing / caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

body.text: Masseter spasm alone after succinylcholine, with no other signs, is not automatically MH — but it warrants stopping triggers, watching EtCO₂ / CK closely, and a low threshold to treat. A known-susceptible patient for elective surgery: use a vapour-free (flushed / activated-charcoal-filtered) machine and TIVA — dantrolene prophylaxis is NOT recommended, just immediately available.
